newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina law to punish cybersex criminals.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina law to punish cybersex criminals.

text.p: A state law goes into effect Sunday that makes it a crime for anyone to use cyberspace to lure children into sex.
Violators of the new law face up to five years in prison if convicted of trying to solicit a child by computer for unlawful sex acts.
The law, passed earlier this year by the North Carolina legislature, goes a step beyond existing laws that make it a crime to take indecent liberties with a minor.
"It's a good law. It clearly defines the different types of behaviour we don't want aimed at our children," said Peter Banks, a director of the National Centre for Missing and Exploited Children.
Earlier this year, FBI agents arrested more than a dozen people accused of using America Online to meet children for sex.
Law enforcement agents are also investigating a convicted child molester in Minnesota who stored the names and addresses of thousands of children inside a prison computer.
